subject: Isolation evidence and routing policy questions
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@healtharc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Isolation evidence and routing policy questions

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a short list of clarifying asks so we can align on the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).

Recap (short):
- HealthArc’s primary driver: strict PHI residency and separation between tenant compute and other customers.
- Two viable paths flagged on the call: Dedicated (reserved GPU pool with customer tenancy) or Private VPC (control plane private, optionally on-prem).
- Procurement looped in for timeline and T&Cs.

Open questions / asks from our side (numbered so they map to evidence):
1) Preferred target: Which deployment do you plan to sign for if ops/security checks are green? (Hosted API not preferred now)
2) Keystore residency: Do you require customer-managed KMS/HSM in your VPC (BYOK) or is Redwood-managed KMS with proven residency acceptable?
3) Network diagrams: please share an updated network diagram showing subnets, peering/VPN, and egress control so our infra team can validate access patterns.
4) Evidence pack: which of the following are must-haves vs nice-to-have — SOC 2 report, encryption at rest attestation, audit log samples, and end-to-end network diagram?
5) Fallback policy: Are you comfortable with automatic fallback to a pinned model variant in another region in case of capacity constraints, or must all traffic strictly remain within the VPC/dedicated pool?
6) PoC schedule: target go/no-go date and an initial traffic profile (peak TPS, avg seq length) for sizing.

Attachments: none from us at this stage — we’ll send a short KMS playbook & routing summary after your network diagram.

Next steps / proposed owners:
- Alex: please send the network diagram + priority evidence list by Friday 4/28.
- Ben (cc’d): will follow up with technical gating questions and a suggested PoC checklist.
- I’ll prepare the mutual action plan and include expected timelines for a Dedicated vs Private VPC onboarding.

Thanks — short and tactical is best here.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@healtharc.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@healtharc.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Isolation evidence and routing policy questions

Hey Stephanie — great recap, appreciate the structure. Answers inline below.

1) Preferred target: Private VPC (control plane in HealthArc account, compute in HealthArc-dedicated subnets) — primary preference. If Redwood can guarantee BYOK + network isolation + signed SLA around egress controls, Dedicated becomes acceptable as a backup.

2) Keystore residency: We require customer-controlled keys for any PHI inference. We can accept an HSM-backed KMS in our cloud account (BYOK). Redwood-managed keys are acceptable only for non-PHI work.

3) Network diagrams: attaching our current diagram (healtharc_network_diag.pdf). It shows our SPA DMZ, private subnets for ML endpoints, and a VPN termination appliance. We can add more detail if you tell us which interfaces you need to validate.

4) Evidence pack priority: Must-haves: SOC 2 Type II, audit log samples for inference requests, proof of KMS BYOK integration (or procedure for HSM key import), and a data-flow diagram. Nice-to-have: internal change control doc.

5) Fallback policy: Strict residency is required for PHI — no automatic cross-region fallback for PHI traffic. For non-PHI traffic we can permit fallback to a pre-approved model in another region (we’d prefer an allowlist mechanism).

6) PoC schedule: Procurement wants a commercial decision by end of May (5/31). PoC can start week of 5/13 if we agree scope this week. Traffic profile for initial PoC: 10 TPS peak, 1–3 s average latency requirement for critical flows, token avg length ~120.

Attachments: healtharc_network_diag.pdf; I’ll follow up with a filled security questionnaire by EOD.

— Alex Turner
Director, Cloud Security
HealthArc
alex.turner@healtharc.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@healtharc.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Apr 2028 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Isolation evidence and routing policy questions

Alex / Stephanie — thanks for the quick turn, Alex. A few technical clarifications and what we’ll provide on the PoC side.

Technical clarifications:
- BYOK/HSM: we support both customer-managed KMS in your account (recommended) and HSM key import workflows. For Private VPC we can configure a CloudKMS key ring in your project and present the server-side decryption underneath the VPC endpoint. I’ll attach our KMS playbook (redwood_kms_playbook.pdf) which outlines the steps and required IAM roles.
- Routing & fallback: we can implement strict routing policies so PHI-tagged requests never leave the VPC/dedicated pool. That requires: (a) request tagging at the app layer or routing rules at the edge, (b) allowlist-only egress. For non-PHI you can enable broader routing and failover.
- Audit logs: we can stream request-level audit logs to your logging endpoint (S3/GCS) with request ids and token counts; sample schema included in the playbook.
- Latency: Dedicated pools have tighter latency SLOs because they avoid multi-tenant scheduling; Private VPC adds a small overhead for networking and BYOK calls — expect ~5–20ms diff depending on HSM round-trips.

PoC proposal (concise):
- Deliverables: 1) Simple canary route within your VPC serving PHI-tagged test traffic; 2) Audit log export to your bucket; 3) KMS BYOK proof-of-concept.
- Duration: 2 weeks for integration, 1 week of soak (3 weeks total).
- Owners: Ben (tech lead), Marissa (solutions owner), HealthArc infra (Alex).
- Required from HealthArc: updated network diag (received), temporary allowlist IP range for test, sample traffic (we can generate based on your profile).

Attachments: redwood_kms_playbook.pdf — contains step-by-step for key import, required roles, and expected latency overhead.

I’ll add a short mutual action plan doc to HubSpot after we confirm dates. If you’re open, I can propose a concrete PoC start date next Tuesday (5/14) to meet your procurement timeline.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
